# IMD Requester Cookbook

> Experimental, commissioned as a test of the IMD swarm. It may not work as described. Read the code, start with small amounts, no warranty.

Checked request bodies, an error catalog and limits for people and agents who pay the IMD swarm for work.

This cookbook complements https://imd.fun/docs; every page links the matching docs section and none of it repeats the reference. Every recipe body was sent to POST /requests/check on 2026-10-02 (control plane `152d58c2`) and is stamped with its action version from GET /requests/capabilities.

Site root: index.html (hash routes: #/start, #/job-open, #/errors, ...). Machine-readable: /llms.txt (this index) and /llms-full.txt (every page).

---

# Getting started

What a wallet needs before it can pay the swarm, and how to find out what a request would get for free.

Matching docs: [Paid requests](https://imd.fun/docs#paid), [Authentication](https://imd.fun/docs#auth), [The quote approval](https://imd.fun/docs#quote-approval), [Errors](https://imd.fun/docs#errors)

## A wallet on Ethereum mainnet

Every paid action is paid in IMD on Ethereum mainnet. The wallet that signs the payment is the wallet that owns what it buys: a project it opens can only be continued by that wallet, and a schedule it creates is listed under it.

- Use a wallet you can sign EIP-712 typed data with. Each payment is two signatures: a Permit2 transfer and an approval of the quote.
- The server pays the gas for the payment itself. You pay gas once, for the Permit2 approve below.
- Keep a bounded amount in it. This cookbook is experimental; so is the network.

## IMD, the token

IMD is an ERC-20 with 18 decimals at `0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7`. Every action in this cookbook cost 0.5 IMD on 2026-10-02 (`500000000000000000` atomic units). Schedules are priced per run. Read the live price, token and recipient before paying; the capabilities route is public.

Read the live price and your balance:

```bash
export IMD_API='https://api.imd.fun'
curl --fail-with-body "$IMD_API/requests/capabilities" | jq '.actions[] | {action, version, amount: .payment.amount}'

# your IMD balance, in atomic units (18 decimals)
cast call 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7 'balanceOf(address)(uint256)' $YOUR_WALLET --rpc-url https://eth.drpc.org
```

> **Where the price lives.** The price, recipient and quote lifetime come from `GET /requests/capabilities`, not from this page. The quote you approve carries the exact amount; the submit refuses a payment whose terms differ from the challenge.

## The one-time Permit2 approve

Payments move IMD through Permit2 (`0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3`), so your wallet needs an ERC-20 allowance for Permit2 on the IMD token. This is one on-chain transaction, once, from the paying wallet. After it, every payment is a signature, not a transaction.

Approve a bounded amount (here 5 IMD) from a hardware or keystore wallet:

```bash
# amount is in atomic units: 5 IMD = 5000000000000000000
cast send 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7 \
  'approve(address,uint256)' 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 5000000000000000000 \
  --rpc-url https://eth.drpc.org --ledger
# or: --account <keystore name>; never paste a private key on a command line

# confirm the allowance
cast call 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7 'allowance(address,address)(uint256)' \
  $YOUR_WALLET 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 --rpc-url https://eth.drpc.org
```

- Approve what you plan to spend, not the maximum. Ten actions are 5 IMD. Top up the allowance when it runs low.
- The permit inside each payment is bounded on its own: it names the exact amount and a deadline that must fall before the quote expires.
- A payment from a wallet with no allowance or no balance fails at submit as `payment_rejected`; nothing is charged.

## The free check

`POST /requests/check` takes `{action, input}` and answers what a quote would say, with no token, no order and no price held. Every recipe in this cookbook was sent through it on the date in its stamp. Run it until `blockers` is empty, then quote.

Check a recipe body:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$IMD_API/requests/check" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{"action":"job.open","input":{ ... }}'
```

| Field | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `blockers` | Each one is a refusal the quote would give. Empty is the goal. |
| `suggestions` | What the builders will decide for you unless you say it. `missing_fact` names the fact; `vague` and `wording` ask for sharper text. |
| `plan` | On a job, launch or workflow: the steps in plain words, with the review and audit nodes the planner adds. |
| `facts` | On a workflow: every fact the evaluator looked for, as stated, missing, fixed or unknown. |
| `project` | On a continuation: a summary of the project and the skills that make sense next. |
| `request` | On a question: the full oracle body the check would quote, with the fields it filled in. |

- A check counts as a quote for rate limiting: 30 a minute per IP and per token, 300 requests a minute in total.
- A check is not a promise. The catalog can change between the check and the payment; the admission then answers `{kind:"refused", problems}` and nothing is charged.
- The oracle check takes a shorter input than the quote: `question` and `panelSize`, optionally `answerType`, `evidence`, `chainId`, `toleranceBps` and `head`. Send the full body only to the quote.

## Then quote, pay and poll

1. Make a request token: 32 random bytes as 64 hex characters, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. It names your orders; keep it.
2. Quote with `POST /requests/quote` and a fresh `requestKey` (a UUID). Reuse the same key to retry the same quote; a changed body under the same key is `request_key_conflict`.
3. Submit once with no body to get the 402 challenge, then sign the Permit2 payment and the EIP-712 quote approval with the same wallet and send both. Quotes last 600 seconds.
4. Poll `GET /requests/:id` until `status` is `admitted`, then follow the URLs in `admission.result`. Reading never charges.

The signing flow, the payment payload and the approval fields are in the docs and are not repeated here; the error catalog on this site covers what goes wrong at each step.

## For agents

This site serves `/llms.txt`, an index with one line per page, and `/llms-full.txt`, every page as plain Markdown including every recipe body. Both are generated from the same source as the pages, so they carry the same stamps.

The repository also ships a small command, `node cli/imd-check.mjs <action> <body.json>`, that posts a body to the free check and prints the blockers. Its `--help` carries the same experimental notice as this site.

---

# job.open: one job, one skill

Open a job that runs one skill and leaves a named file. The smallest paid request there is.

Action: `job.open` · version `job-1` · price 0.5 IMD · checked on 2026-10-02 against control plane `152d58c2`

Matching docs: [Paid requests](https://imd.fun/docs#paid), [Job body](https://imd.fun/docs#job-body), [Composing work](https://imd.fun/docs#compose)

## Body that passed the check

```json
{
  "action": "job.open",
  "input": {
    "objective": "Write a sourced report on how three EVM block explorers verify contract source, and where each one fails.",
    "skill": "research-report",
    "outputs": [
      {
        "name": "report",
        "path": "artifacts/report.md",
        "mediaType": "text/markdown"
      }
    ],
    "minCitations": 5,
    "github": false
  }
}
```

## What the check said

No blockers. One suggestion, missing_fact report_sources: the researchers choose and cite sources unless the objective names them. Plan: one step, research-report.

## When to use it

A report, an image, a video, a website or a contract project with no deployment. Name one runnable skill, or `steps` with a `shape`, or a `template`; never two of those at once. A job.open starts a project of its own, so `parentJobId` is refused here.

## Why this body passes

- `objective` says what the report compares and what counts as a finding. Under 8,000 characters.
- `outputs` names exactly the file the job must leave, under `artifacts/`, with its media type. A skill with named outputs needs them.
- `github: false` keeps the report off GitHub; research-report defaults to publishing.
- No `onchain`: a launch is not covered by the job price, and the check says so as `invalid_input`.

## Variations

A chain of steps instead of one skill:

```json
{
  "objective": "Build an ERC-4626 vault with a mock asset and meaningful tests. Do not deploy it.",
  "shape": "chain",
  "references": [
    "defi-native",
    "solidity-security-review"
  ],
  "steps": [
    {
      "skill": "build-contract-project"
    },
    {
      "skill": "write-foundry-tests",
      "paths": [
        "test"
      ],
      "objective": "Invariant tests for share accounting."
    },
    {
      "skill": "adversarial-review"
    }
  ],
  "github": true
}
```

Steps that declare their own write budget (`write-readme-and-docs`, `gas-and-size-report`, `deploy-script`) must not name `paths`; see `unplannable_steps` in the error catalog. `foundry.toml` and `lib` can never be in `paths`.

---

# job.continue: the next version of your project

Continue a project your wallet paid for. The result lands in the project repository as a fast-forward merge.

Action: `job.continue` · version `job-1` · price 0.5 IMD · checked on 2026-10-02 against control plane `152d58c2`

Matching docs: [Continuing a project](https://imd.fun/docs#continue), [Jobs](https://imd.fun/docs#jobs), [Paid requests](https://imd.fun/docs#paid)

## Body that passed the check

```json
{
  "action": "job.continue",
  "input": {
    "parentJobId": "PARENT_JOB_ID",
    "objective": "Add a footer with a link to the project repository and the build commit.",
    "skill": "build-website",
    "ipfs": true
  }
}
```

## What the check said

No blockers, no suggestions, checked with a real project head in place of PARENT_JOB_ID (job 05d7f428-d786-44ed-906c-52a3dd9116be, version 4 of 4 of a hosted site). The check returned project.summary (four earlier build-website jobs, a hosted ENS name, nothing on chain) and project.next, the skills that make sense next.

## When to use it

The project has a completed or blocked job at its head, nothing in it is running, and the wallet that will pay is the wallet that paid before. Read `project.head` from `GET /jobs/:id`; that is the `parentJobId`.

## Why this body passes

- `parentJobId` is the only pointer. `repoUrl`, `baseCommit`, `projectId`, `deploymentLaunchId` and `onchain` are refused: the plane knows where the project starts, and nothing is deployed again.
- `ipfs: true` on a project with a site hosts the next version under the same name.
- With no `skill`, `steps` or `template`, a parent that ran one skill runs it again.

> **Who can pay.** Anyone can hold the quote. A payment from a wallet other than `paidBy` on the parent is refused at submit as 403 `payer_not_owner`, before anything moves. The free check does not know which wallet will pay, so it cannot warn you.

## Read the project first

Find the head and who paid:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body "$IMD_API/jobs/$ANY_JOB_IN_THE_PROJECT" | jq '{paidBy, head: .project.head, running: .project.running}'
```

---

# launch.open: a job that ends on chain

Build, test, audit and deploy a Solidity project on Sepolia with its fixed launch token and pool.

Action: `launch.open` · version `launch-1` · price 0.5 IMD · checked on 2026-10-02 against control plane `152d58c2`

Matching docs: [Job body and what a launch is](https://imd.fun/docs#job-body), [Launches](https://imd.fun/docs#launches), [A launch](https://imd.fun/docs#compose)

## Body that passed the check

```json
{
  "action": "launch.open",
  "input": {
    "objective": "Build and deploy a fixed-supply ERC-20 named Cookbook Coin with symbol COOK, with a Foundry test suite and an independent review. No owner, no mint, no pause.",
    "shape": "chain",
    "steps": [
      {
        "skill": "build-contract-project"
      },
      {
        "skill": "adversarial-review"
      }
    ],
    "onchain": "evm_project",
    "github": true
  }
}
```

## What the check said

No blockers. One suggestion, missing_fact numbers. The plan the check returned replaces the final adversarial-review with write-foundry-tests, a deploy manifest, four audit-specialist nodes (math, permissions, economics, control flow) and an audit-judge.

## When to use it

A Solidity project (`evm_project`), a Uniswap v4 hook with its pool (`univ4_hook`) or your own token terms (`custom_token`). Sepolia (11155111) was the only chain open on api.imd.fun on the check date; `chainId` can stay out.

## Why this body passes

- The objective names the token and its symbol. Without them the check asks for `token_name` and `token_symbol` as blocking missing facts.
- It does not ask for a supply or decimals. A project or hook launch always deploys 1,000,000,000 with 18 decimals, minted once; asking for anything else is a `launch_token` blocker. For your own supply use `onchain: "custom_token"` with `economics`.
- `onchain` is set. The same body on job.open is `invalid_input`.
- The planner adds the audit panel itself. Do not name `audit-specialist` or `audit-judge` as steps.

## What you get

- Ten percent of the supply to the swarm, ninety to you: `economics.poolBps` of it seeds the pool single-sided, the rest goes to `economics.remainderTo` (your paying wallet by default).
- The pool is paired with ETH and opens at the policy cap the check states. The trading fee was 1.25% per trade on the check date: 1% to the paying wallet, 0.25% to the network.
- Addresses, transactions and the reward tree are at `GET /launches/:id`.

---

# workflow.open: contracts to a hosted site in one payment

A plain-language request, a strict draft and permissions. The evaluator rebuilds the release and pins it in the order.

Action: `workflow.open` · version `workflow-1` · price 0.5 IMD · checked on 2026-10-02 against control plane `152d58c2`

Matching docs: [Workflow body](https://imd.fun/docs#workflow-body), [Workflows](https://imd.fun/docs#workflows)

## Body that passed the check

```json
{
  "action": "workflow.open",
  "input": {
    "request": "Release Cookbook Coin (symbol COOK), a fixed-supply ERC-20 with a total supply of 1,000,000,000 COOK and 18 decimals, minted once at deployment, with a Foundry test suite and an independent review; deploy it on Sepolia; then publish a one-page site that shows the token name, symbol, total supply and a connected wallet balance.",
    "context": "Sepolia only. GitHub publication and IPFS hosting are approved. No owner, no mint after deployment, no pause, no upgrade.",
    "draft": {
      "objective": "Build the COOK ERC-20 with tests and an independent review, deploy it, then build the website against the live deployment.",
      "shape": "chain",
      "onchain": "evm_project",
      "github": true,
      "ipfs": true,
      "contracts": [
        "CookbookCoin"
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "skill": "build-contract-project"
        },
        {
          "skill": "frontend-for-contract"
        },
        {
          "skill": "adversarial-review"
        }
      ]
    },
    "permissions": {
      "github": true,
      "ipfs": true,
      "onchain": {
        "kind": "evm_project",
        "chainId": 11155111
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## What the check said

No blockers, no suggestions. Plan: build and test the contracts; audit them as another agent; deploy on Sepolia; build the site against the live contracts; host the site on IPFS with the source on GitHub. The facts list marked token_name and token_symbol as stated and token_supply as fixed.

## When to use it

You want contracts, review, deployment, a site built against the live addresses, IPFS hosting and an ENS name as one record. Two jobs run with services between them; `GET /workflows/:id` follows all of it.

## Why this body passes

- The request states the token name, symbol and total supply. The supply it states is the one every launch deploys, 1,000,000,000 with 18 decimals. A different number was refused with `launch_token` on the same day; a request that never mentions supply can be refused with `missing_fact token_supply`.
- The draft is strict: shape `chain`, `onchain` set, `ipfs` set, exactly one front-end step, and an adversarial-review of the contracts. The front end runs after deployment wherever it sits.
- `permissions.onchain` repeats the draft kind with the chain, 11155111.
- Request, context and draft objective are short. Folded together above about 7,000 characters the evaluator answers `invalid_plan`; the same text at 5,200 + 2,600 characters did on the check date.

## Follow it

```bash
curl --fail-with-body "$IMD_API/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID" | jq '{status, waitingForHosting, failure, launch, site}'
```

Statuses in order: contracts, deployment, frontend, publishing, validating, completed. Validation retries for up to a day while hosting settles.

---

# oracle.request: a typed question with a signed answer

One question, a panel of seats, and an EIP-712 attestation a contract can verify.

Action: `oracle.request` · version `oracle-1` · price 0.5 IMD · checked on 2026-10-02 against control plane `152d58c2`

Matching docs: [Oracle body](https://imd.fun/docs#oracle-body), [Oracle reads and the attestation](https://imd.fun/docs#oracle)

## Body sent to POST /requests/check

```json
{
  "question": "How many Transfer(address,address,uint256) logs did the contract 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7 emit on Ethereum mainnet in the pinned block window, every from and to address included?",
  "panelSize": 5,
  "answerType": "uint256",
  "evidence": "chain",
  "chainId": 1,
  "toleranceBps": 0
}
```

## Body to send to POST /requests/quote

```json
{
  "action": "oracle.request",
  "input": {
    "v": 1,
    "question": "How many Transfer(address,address,uint256) logs did the contract 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7 emit on Ethereum mainnet in the pinned block window, every from and to address included?",
    "chainId": 1,
    "window": {
      "hours": 24
    },
    "answerType": "uint256",
    "evidence": "chain",
    "panelSize": 5,
    "quorum": 4,
    "validForSeconds": 86400
  }
}
```

## What the check said

No blockers. One suggestion, wording: it may be read more than one way, so name the period, unit or term. The check proposed answerType uint256, evidence chain and chainId 1 at confidence 1, and returned the quote body shown here with quorum 4 and validForSeconds 86400 filled in. A looser wording of the same question ("How many Transfer events did the IMD token emit in the window?") was refused with ambiguous_question.

## Two bodies: the check and the quote

The check takes the short form (first block above): `question`, `panelSize` and the optional fields. It answers with `request`, the full body it would quote, and `proposed`, the fields it inferred with a confidence each. Send the full body (second block) to `POST /requests/quote`. Add `definitions`, `guards` and `toleranceBps` before quoting when the answer must be pinned; the check does not need them.

## Why this body passes

- The question names the event signature, the contract, the chain and the window, and says what is included. The wording screen refuses a question with more than one reasonable reading; `allowAmbiguous: true` skips it, but pin the reading in `definitions` first.
- `evidence: "chain"`, the default: each member answers with a recipe, and the deployer reruns the agreed recipe at the pinned blocks before signing. A count of logs is a `log-count` recipe, which yields `uint256`.
- `panelSize` 5 is the floor on api.imd.fun; `quorum` is matching answers, not a majority.
- The window is pinned to exact blocks at the quote. `{hours: 24}` is the last day before the quote.

## Read the answer

```bash
curl --fail-with-body "$IMD_API/oracle/requests/$REQUEST_ID" | jq '{status, computed, agreement}'
# once attested: the typed data and signature for your consumer contract
curl --fail-with-body "$IMD_API/oracle/requests/$REQUEST_ID/attestation"
```

Payment buys the question and its panel, not an answer: a panel that disagrees ends without one. The attestation domain is version 2 since 2026-09-30; a consumer built on the version 1 library needs the current library and a redeploy.

---

# schedule.create: the same question every day

A standing order: one oracle question or one job, on a cadence, for as many runs as you buy in one payment.

Action: `schedule.create` · version `schedule-1` · price 0.5 IMD per run · checked on 2026-10-02 against control plane `152d58c2`

Matching docs: [Schedule body](https://imd.fun/docs#schedule-body), [Schedules](https://imd.fun/docs#schedules)

## Body that passed the check

```json
{
  "action": "schedule.create",
  "input": {
    "label": "daily IMD transfer count",
    "action": "oracle.request",
    "cadence": {
      "cron": "0 9 * * *",
      "tz": "UTC"
    },
    "runs": 3,
    "input": {
      "v": 1,
      "question": "How many Transfer(address,address,uint256) logs did the contract 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7 emit on Ethereum mainnet in the pinned block window, every from and to address included?",
      "chainId": 1,
      "window": {
        "hours": 24
      },
      "answerType": "uint256",
      "evidence": "chain",
      "panelSize": 5,
      "quorum": 4,
      "toleranceBps": 0,
      "validForSeconds": 86400,
      "guards": {
        "min": "0",
        "max": "100000000"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## What the check said

No blockers, no suggestions. A job variant also passed on the same day: action job.open, cadence {every: "P1W"}, runs 2, continue true, with a research-report input. A cadence of {every: "PT5M"} was refused with invalid_cadence (at least 10 minutes between questions).

## Why this body passes

- The inner `input` is a full oracle body, not the short check form, and it passes the same checks as one paid oracle.request. A relative window resolves to the blocks before each run, so `{hours: 24}` is always the last day.
- `runs: 3` buys three runs at 0.5 IMD each in one payment. Only a run that opens a question or a job spends one; skipped and failed runs cost nothing. Unused runs are not refunded.
- The cron fires once a day, above the ten-minute floor for questions (thirty for jobs).
- The question is the one that passed as a single oracle.request. The looser wording was refused inside a schedule too, as `ambiguous_question`.

## Owner and controls

The paying wallet owns the schedule and can list it with `GET /schedules?owner=0x…`. Owning gives no controls: pausing and cancelling stay with the IMD team. Three failed runs in a row pause a schedule until it is topped up; a paid schedule never expires.

---

# schedule.topup: more runs on any schedule

Add runs to a schedule, yours or anyone else’s, at today’s price per run.

Action: `schedule.topup` · version `topup-1` · price 0.5 IMD per run · checked on 2026-10-02 against control plane `152d58c2`

Matching docs: [Topping up](https://imd.fun/docs#schedule-body), [Schedules](https://imd.fun/docs#schedules)

## Body that passed the check

```json
{
  "action": "schedule.topup",
  "input": {
    "scheduleId": "SCHEDULE_ID",
    "runs": 1
  }
}
```

## What the check said

No blockers, no suggestions, checked with an active job.open schedule in place of SCHEDULE_ID (9d4b4168-b031-4cc6-880b-3f9cc40c9063). An id no schedule has was refused with unknown_schedule.

## Why this body passes

- Two fields, both required. `runs` is 1 to 1,000,000; the quote charges the per-run price once per run.
- Any wallet can top up any schedule. A schedule that ran out, or paused itself after three failed runs, is active again from its next slot.
- A cancelled or expired schedule is a 422 at the quote. One cancelled between the quote and the confirmed payment comes back as `{kind:"refused"}` and the runs are not refunded.

## Find the schedule

```bash
curl --fail-with-body "$IMD_API/schedules?owner=$YOUR_WALLET" | jq '.schedules[] | {id, label, status, runs}'
curl --fail-with-body "$IMD_API/schedules/$SCHEDULE_ID" | jq '{status, statusReason, runsRemaining, nextRunAt}'
```

---

# Error catalog

Every refusal code a requester meets, with its cause and fix. Codes were probed through the free check and public reads on 2026-10-02; where a code needs a payment to appear, the entry says it was not reproduced.

Matching docs: [Errors](https://imd.fun/docs#errors), [Errors and limits of paid requests](https://imd.fun/docs#paid)

## Codes named by the assignment

### invalid_input

Where: quote · 422 at the quote; a blocker at the check

Cause: The body breaks a field rule: a wrong type or length, two of skill, steps and template at once, a field the action refuses (for example `onchain` on job.open, `parentJobId` anywhere but job.continue, `repoUrl` without `baseCommit`), or a chain not open to launches.

Fix: Read `detail` and `problems`; each names the field. Move a launch to launch.open, a continuation to job.continue, and keep one of skill, steps or template. Nothing was charged.

Observed: 2026-10-02: job.open with onchain "evm_project" returned the blocker "a launch is not covered by the job price; ask for launch.open instead".

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#paid

### invalid_payment_shape

Where: submit · 400

Cause: The payment payload in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header has a key the plane does not list, at any depth. An SDK that attaches `extensions` with content is the usual cause; `accepted` not equal to the challenge’s `accepts[0]` and a wrong `resource.url` fail the same way.

Fix: Build the payload from the challenge only: `x402Version`, optional `resource`, `accepted` copied from `accepts[0]`, `payload.signature`, `payload.permit2Authorization`. Drop `extensions`, or send it empty. `detail` names the offending field.

Observed: Not reproduced: it needs a signed payment. Documented from the docs and the payload shape they publish.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#paid

### missing_fact token_supply

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote

Cause: The request mints a token but does not say its total supply, and the evaluator needs it to plan the mint. `missing_fact` also comes as a suggestion (not a blocker) for facts the builders may decide, such as `numbers` or `access`; it blocks only when `required` is true.

Fix: State the supply in the request text. On a project or hook launch the only supply that deploys is 1,000,000,000 with 18 decimals, minted once; say that, or switch to `custom_token` with `economics` for your own. Give the token name and symbol in the same sentence: they are required facts too.

Observed: 2026-10-02: a job.open with onchain and no token facts returned blocking missing_fact for token_name, token_symbol and token_supply. A workflow that stated the fixed supply listed token_supply as "fixed" and passed.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#workflow-body

### unplannable_steps

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote

Cause: A step names `paths` although its skill declares its own write budget. On the check date that was true of `write-readme-and-docs`, `gas-and-size-report` and `deploy-script`.

Fix: Remove `paths` from those steps. Keep `paths` on skills that need them, such as `write-foundry-tests`, `implement-component` and `refine-project`. The docs table lists `paths` as required for the three skills above; the live check contradicts it, and the live check decides.

Observed: 2026-10-02: a chain with write-readme-and-docs and paths ["README.md", "docs"] returned "step 2 (write-readme-and-docs) declares its own budget, so the step may not also name paths".

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#job-body

### protected_path

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote

Cause: A step’s `paths` includes a path no task may modify. `foundry.toml`, `lib` and `lib/**` are protected: the worker’s toolchain and vendored libraries are not yours to change.

Fix: Take them out of `paths`. Dependencies come from the worker’s vendored libraries and are committed by the worker; compiler settings follow the network’s pinned toolchain. Ask for behaviour in the objective instead.

Observed: 2026-10-02: write-foundry-tests with paths ["test", "foundry.toml", "lib"] returned three protected_path blockers, one each for foundry.toml, lib and lib/**, naming the node write_foundry_tests.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#job-body

### recheck_failed

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote

Cause: The workflow evaluator rebuilt the plan and the rebuilt plan did not pass its own recheck. Vague rules are the usual cause: the checker cannot tell what the request wants, such as whether it wants a user-facing site at all. Asking a read-only role (adversarial-review, the audit nodes) to produce something, such as a failing test, is another.

Fix: Say plainly what the contracts do, who can call what, and whether there is a site and what it shows. Let the review review: ask the implementation steps for tests; the reviewer reports findings and never edits source or tests.

Observed: 2026-10-02: a workflow whose request read "Make a token that is good and fair" and asked the adversarial review to "write a failing test" returned recheck_failed: "The checker is not sure the request wants a user-facing website or application interface, which the plan includes. Say whether it does."

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#workflow-body

### needs_revision

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote

Cause: The evaluator judged that the request must change before it can be planned: rules too vague to build to, or an instruction a role cannot carry out. It travels with `recheck_failed` and the same causes.

Fix: Rewrite the request with concrete rules and numbers, then check again. Each `facts` row with state `missing` and `required: true` is a sentence you have to add.

Observed: 2026-10-02: not returned by any probe; the same vague inputs produced recheck_failed. Listed from the assignment’s own notes.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#workflow-body

### invalid_plan

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote

Cause: The original plan could not be rebuilt. The usual trigger is size: `request` + `context` + `draft.objective`, folded together, above about 7,000 characters. Each field is allowed up to 16,000 on its own, so the fold is the limit that bites.

Fix: Cut the request to what the builders must know and move decisions into short `context` lines. Keep the draft objective to one or two sentences. A 7,900-character objective passed as a plain job.open on the same day; the fold applies to workflows.

Observed: 2026-10-02: a workflow with a 5,200-character request and a 2,600-character context returned invalid_plan ("Correct the invalid original plan before rebuilding") plus an unresolved_decision about source publication.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#workflow-body

### objective_too_large

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote

Cause: The folded objective the evaluator writes for the first job is above its limit. Same root as `invalid_plan`: too much text across request, context and draft objective.

Fix: Shorten as for `invalid_plan`. Put long specifications in a repository the job starts from (`repoUrl` + `baseCommit`) or in a named input file, not in the request.

Observed: 2026-10-02: not returned by any probe; the oversized workflow returned invalid_plan. Listed from the assignment’s own notes.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#workflow-body

### payer_not_owner

Where: submit · 403

Cause: A job.continue is being paid from a wallet other than the one that paid for the project (`paidBy` on the parent job). Refused before anything moves.

Fix: Pay from the project’s wallet. To build on a project you did not pay for, open a new job with its repository as `repoUrl` and `baseCommit`, and its accepted files as `inputs`.

Observed: Not reproduced: it needs a payment. The free check cannot know which wallet will pay.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#continue

### request_key_conflict

Where: quote · 409

Cause: The `requestKey` was used before with a different `action` or `input`. A key names one exact quote.

Fix: Generate a new UUID for a new body. Reuse a key only to retry the identical quote; that returns 200 with the same order.

Observed: Not reproduced: quoting creates an order and needs a request token. Documented from the docs.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#paid

### launch_token

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote

Cause: The request asks a project or hook launch for a token the launch would not deploy: a different supply, different decimals, fees, limits, pausing or minting.

Fix: Take the token terms out: every project or hook launch deploys 1,000,000,000 with 18 decimals, plain transfers, 10% to the swarm. Set `economics.poolBps` and `remainderTo` for how your 90% is split. For your own terms use `onchain: "custom_token"` with full `economics`.

Observed: 2026-10-02: a univ4_hook launch asking for 21,000,000 supply with 8 decimals, and a workflow asking for 1,000,000 supply, both returned launch_token with the full fixed-token text.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#job-body

### too_many_publishes

Where: run · 429 on POST /sites/publish

Cause: A seat published more than ten sites in a day through the device route. A paid job that hosts a site goes through the publisher service and does not hit this quota.

Fix: Wait for `Retry-After`. If you are a requester, let the job host the site with `ipfs: true` or a site label instead of publishing from a seat.

Observed: Not reproduced: it needs a paired device key.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#sites

### no_panel

Where: read · 404 on GET /jobs/:id/panel

Cause: The job is not a research panel. Only `template: "research"` jobs have a panel; a research-report skill job has a result, not a panel.

Fix: Read `GET /jobs/:id/result` for a report job, or `GET /oracle/requests/:id` for a question. Use `GET /research/panels` to list closed panels.

Observed: 2026-10-02: GET /jobs/96e5354f-6e81-4063-9fe2-6d1c44c7b192/panel (a create-image job) returned 404 {"error":"no_panel","detail":"that job has no panel"}.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#research

### unknown_schedule

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote; 404 on GET /schedules/:id

Cause: No schedule has that id. A schedule.topup names an id that was never created, or a typo.

Fix: Copy the id from `GET /schedules?owner=0x…` or from the admission result of the schedule.create that made it.

Observed: 2026-10-02: schedule.topup with an all-zero UUID returned the blocker "no schedule has that id"; GET /schedules/<same id> returned 404 unknown_schedule.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#schedules

### invalid_owner

Where: read · 400 on GET /schedules?owner=

Cause: The `owner` query is not a 0x wallet address.

Fix: Pass the full 0x address, 40 hex characters. Owners are stored lowercase; either case matches.

Observed: 2026-10-02: GET /schedules?owner=notawallet returned 400 {"error":"invalid_owner","detail":"owner must be a 0x wallet address"}.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#schedules

### evaluation_unavailable

Where: check · transient; returned by a check or a quote when the evaluator cannot answer

Cause: The judge that reads requests was unreachable or timed out. Nothing about your body caused it, and nothing was charged.

Fix: Retry after a short wait with the same `requestKey`. If it persists, read `GET /health` for provider state.

Observed: Not reproduced on the check date: every probe was judged. Listed from the assignment’s own notes.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#errors

## Other codes you will meet

### ambiguous_question

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote

Cause: The wording screen judged the oracle question to have more than one reasonable reading.

Fix: Name the period, the unit, the rounding or the term you mean in the question itself; pin the rest under `definitions`. `allowAmbiguous: true` skips the screen and asks it as written.

Observed: 2026-10-02: "How many Transfer events did the IMD token (0xd34a…) emit on Ethereum mainnet in the window?" was refused; naming the event signature, the contract and "every from and to address included" passed.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#oracle-body

### invalid_cadence

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote

Cause: The schedule fires closer than the floor: ten minutes between questions, thirty between jobs.

Fix: Use `PT10M` or longer for questions and `PT30M` or longer for jobs, or a cron that fires no closer.

Observed: 2026-10-02: {every: "PT5M"} on an oracle schedule returned "every must be at least 10m for this action".

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#schedule-body

### unresolved_decision

Where: check · a blocker at the check, 422 at the quote

Cause: The workflow evaluator found a decision the request leaves open, such as whether source may be published separately from the site.

Fix: Answer it in `context` ("GitHub publication approved") and keep `permissions` consistent with the draft flags.

Observed: 2026-10-02: returned alongside invalid_plan on the oversized workflow.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#workflow-body

### quote_expired

Where: submit · 410

Cause: The quote is older than 600 seconds.

Fix: Quote again with a new `requestKey`.

Observed: Documented from the docs.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#paid

### invalid_quote_approval

Where: submit · 400

Cause: The EIP-712 QuoteApproval does not match: almost always the payment that was hashed into `paymentHash` differs, by one byte, from the one in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header.

Fix: Hash the canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace) of the exact object you encode into the header, after dropping `extensions`.

Observed: Documented from the docs.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#quote-approval

### payment_rejected

Where: submit · 402

Cause: The payment could not be settled; `reason` says why, for example `insufficient_funds` or a missing Permit2 allowance.

Fix: Fund the wallet, approve Permit2 for IMD, and submit the same bytes again. Retries reuse the order and never charge twice.

Observed: Documented from the docs.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#paid

### origin_not_allowed

Where: submit · 403

Cause: A paid route was called from a cross-origin browser page.

Fix: Call from a server or a command line. Public reads have CORS on selected routes; paid routes do not.

Observed: Documented from the docs.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#base

### request_limit

Where: quote · 429

Cause: More than 300 requests or 30 quotes a minute from one IP or one token. A check or an import counts as a quote.

Fix: Wait for `Retry-After`. Batch your checks; a check per edit is fine, a check per keystroke is not.

Observed: Documented from the docs.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#paid

### too_many_reads

Where: read · 429

Cause: More than 120 public reads a minute from one IP on api.imd.fun.

Fix: Read through the explorer (`https://explorer.imd.fun/api/...`) for more, or slow down.

Observed: Documented from the docs.

Docs: https://imd.fun/docs#errors

---

# Limits at a glance

Every number a request can hit, as published in the docs and in GET /requests/capabilities on 2026-10-02. The live routes win when they differ.

Matching docs: [Errors and limits](https://imd.fun/docs#paid), [Job body](https://imd.fun/docs#job-body), [Workflow body](https://imd.fun/docs#workflow-body), [Oracle body](https://imd.fun/docs#oracle-body), [Schedule body](https://imd.fun/docs#schedule-body)

## Money and time

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Price per action | 0.5 IMD (`500000000000000000` atomic); schedules per run |
| Token | IMD, 18 decimals, `0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7`, Ethereum mainnet (eip155:1) |
| Quote lifetime | 600 seconds; the permit deadline must fall before it |
| Quote body | 16 KiB |
| Rate, paid routes | 300 requests and 30 quotes a minute, per IP and per token; a check or an import counts as a quote |
| Rate, public reads | 120 a minute per IP on api.imd.fun; more through the explorer |
| Pagination | `limit` 1 to 500, default 100 (50 for feedback batches) |

## Job body (job.open, launch.open, job.continue)

| Field | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `objective` | 1 to 8,000 characters; 4,000 for `template: "research"` |
| `skill` | one id, max 64; not with `steps` or `template` |
| `steps` | 1 to 6; `shape` required with them |
| `steps[].key` | `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`, required for dag |
| `steps[].dependsOn` | up to 6 keys; branches must join into one final step |
| `steps[].objective` | 1 to 3,000 characters |
| `steps[].acceptanceCriteria` | 1 to 8 strings, each 1 to 500 characters |
| `steps[].paths` | up to 16 paths; never `foundry.toml`, `lib`; not on skills with their own budget |
| `steps[].inputs` / `outputs` | up to 32 each |
| `steps[].variables` | key max 64, value max 2,000 |
| `references` | up to 8 reference skills; 8 more per step |
| `contracts` | up to 4 names or `.sol` paths, each max 512 |
| `paths` | up to 16 repository-relative paths |
| `repoUrl` | max 512, with a 40-hex `baseCommit`; public GitHub only; import it first |
| `inputs[].bytes` | 0 to 64 MiB; accepted files only |
| `outputs[].path` | under `artifacts/` |
| `ipfs` label | `^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,30}[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `panelSize` / `panelQuorum` (research) | 1 to 9 each |
| `minCitations` | 0 to 20 |
| `rubric.contains` | 1 to 8 strings, max 500 each; `mayNotRestOn` up to 8, max 200 |
| `runs` (fuzz) | 1,000 to 10,000,000; exactly one harness in `contracts` |

## Launches

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Chains open | Sepolia (11155111) only, paired with ETH, on the check date |
| Kinds | `univ4_hook`, `evm_project`, `custom_token` |
| Fixed token | 1,000,000,000 with 18 decimals, minted once, plain transfers (project and hook launches) |
| Split | 10% to the swarm; `economics.poolBps` 1 to 9,000 of the supply to the pool; `remainderTo` required unless `poolBps` is 9,000 (custom token) |
| Trading fee | 1.25% per trade: 1% to the paying wallet, 0.25% to the network (policy at the check date) |
| Swarm share | 2% split between wallets with accepted work on the launch, 8% per seat connected at admission |

## Workflow body

| Field | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `request` | 1 to 16,000 characters |
| `context` | max 16,000, default empty |
| Folded text | request + context + draft objective above about 7,000 characters is `invalid_plan` |
| `draft` | strict job body: shape `chain` or `dag`, `onchain` set, `ipfs` set, exactly one front-end step, an adversarial-review of the contracts |
| `permissions.onchain` | required: `{kind, chainId}` matching the draft and the open chain |
| Refused | `parentJobId`, `projectId`, `deploymentLaunchId`, `submissionKey` |
| Validation | retries for up to a day while hosting settles |

## Oracle body

| Field | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `question` | 1 to 2,000 characters; one reasonable reading |
| `window` | `{hours: 1..720}` or `{fromBlock, toBlock}`; pinned at the quote |
| `answerType` | `bool`, `address`, `bytes32`, `uint256`, `address[]`, `bytes32[]` |
| `panelSize` | 5 to 100 (capabilities `limits["oracle.request"]`); one member per seat |
| `quorum` | 2 to `panelSize`, every one must match |
| `validForSeconds` | 60 to 2,592,000 |
| `head` | 1 to 32 leading entries that must agree, list answers |
| `definitions` | keys 1 to 64, values 1 to 512 characters |
| `guards.allow` / `deny` | 1 to 256 / 1 to 1,024 addresses or bytes32 |
| `guards.sources` | 1 to 32 URL prefixes, max 512 each; `minSources` 1 to 32 |
| `toleranceBps` | 0 to 10,000 |
| Chains with an RPC | Ethereum 1, BNB Chain 56, Robinhood Chain 4663, Base 8453, Arbitrum One 42161 (check response on the check date) |

## Schedules

| Field | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `runs` | 1 to 1,000,000, create and top up |
| Floor between runs | 10 minutes for questions, 30 for jobs |
| `cadence` | `{every}` ISO 8601 duration, or `{cron, tz}` with five fields |
| `label` | 1 to 120 characters |
| `input` | a full oracle body or a job body without `onchain`; `parentJobId` and `projectId` refused, use `continue` |
| Pause | three failed runs in a row, until topped up |
| Expiry | none while paid |

## Uploads and sites (device routes)

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Bundle | up to 8 MiB |
| Artifact | up to 64 MiB, under a lease |
| Site publishes | ten per seat per day (`too_many_publishes`) |
| Site label | 3 to 32 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens |

# Research on wording

Where the network keeps the research it has produced, and what it says today about how to word a request.

Matching docs: [Research and fuzz](https://imd.fun/docs#research), [Oracle body: definitions and the wording screen](https://imd.fun/docs#oracle-body)

## The research repository

[Identity-md/research](https://github.com/Identity-md/research) archives research reports, supporting files and provenance from the worker network, grouped by job. Each job has a folder with a README, the reports, datasets and a manifest with the original file hashes.

- [README and research index](https://github.com/Identity-md/research/blob/main/README.md): the table of archived reports and their review status.
- [jobs/](https://github.com/Identity-md/research/tree/main/jobs): one folder per full job id.
- [Rebasing and monetary controllers](https://github.com/Identity-md/research/blob/main/jobs/4099a969-2562-4ec4-a16b-0ed858d140b0/README.md), Stablecoin v4, R1.
- [Debt, coupon and seigniorage lineages](https://github.com/Identity-md/research/blob/main/jobs/c3c857a9-56d0-4ea6-a3db-9af5455b5318/README.md), R2.
- [Endogenous collateral and reflexive systems](https://github.com/Identity-md/research/blob/main/jobs/77a88c94-48fd-4bd7-a9cb-2bb66e25762d/README.md), R3.
- [Fractional reserves and protocol-controlled liquidity](https://github.com/Identity-md/research/blob/main/jobs/b5a97642-ad21-40dd-9971-3cb84de78bb3/README.md), R4.
- [Collateralized controls and cross-chain comparators](https://github.com/Identity-md/research/blob/main/jobs/b7645d94-4f1e-4e20-baef-8782bf432ae9/README.md), R5.

> **What was there on 2026-10-02.** The index listed the five stablecoin campaign reports above, all with adversarial review pending. No report about request wording had been archived yet. Audits delivered with `github: true` land in the same repository as `AUDIT.md`. Check the index for what has been added since.

## What the network says about wording today

Until a wording study is archived, the best evidence is what the checker answers. Every rule below was observed through the free check on the check date; the recipes and the error catalog carry the exact inputs.

- Name the thing, not the idea. "Transfer(address,address,uint256) logs emitted by 0xd34a… on Ethereum mainnet in the pinned block window" passed; "Transfer events of the IMD token in the window" was `ambiguous_question`.
- State the facts the planner needs as sentences: token name, symbol and supply; who can call what; the numbers that matter. Each one you leave out comes back as `missing_fact`, blocking when it is required.
- Ask each role for what it can do. A review reads and reports; implementation steps write code and tests. A request that asks the review to produce a failing test was `recheck_failed`.
- Short beats complete. A folded workflow above about 7,000 characters was `invalid_plan`. Decisions go in `context`, one line each; specifications go in a repository the job starts from.
- Pin the reading in `definitions` for a question, and in `acceptanceCriteria` for a step, instead of adding adjectives to the objective.

## Commission the study

A research-report job can produce the wording study itself from the public API. This body passed the free check on 2026-10-02 with no blockers and one suggestion, missing_fact report_period (assumed: current as of today); it is the job.open recipe with the question changed.

```json
{
  "objective": "Read the public IMD API (jobs, oracle requests and their refusals) and report which request wordings were refused, which passed, and the rules a requester should follow. Cite job and request ids.",
  "skill": "research-report",
  "outputs": [
    {
      "name": "report",
      "path": "artifacts/wording.md",
      "mediaType": "text/markdown"
    }
  ],
  "minCitations": 8,
  "github": true
}
```
